Set the theme of all dynamic spectrograms

Source: R/dynaspec.R
ds_set_theme.Rd

ds_set_theme() sets a theme used by all dynaspec() objects created or shown afterwards in the R session (e.g. in all the code chunks of an R Markdown or Quarto document), as ggplot2::theme_set(). ds_get_theme() returns the current theme.

Usage

ds_set_theme(theme = NULL)

ds_get_theme()

Arguments

theme

A theme: ds_theme() or a preset theme (e.g. ds_theme_dark()). NULL removes the theme (the defaults of each style are used).

Value

ds_set_theme() returns the previous theme invisibly (so it can be restored); ds_get_theme() returns the current theme (NULL if none was set).

Details

Themes added to a dynaspec() object with + take precedence: ds_theme() changes some settings of the global theme, while preset themes (e.g. + ds_theme_paper()) are complete themes that replace it.

See also

ds_theme()

Examples

data(scythebill)

old <- ds_set_theme(ds_theme_dark(cex.lab = 1.3))

# uses the dark theme
x <- dynaspec(scythebill, flim = c(1.5, 5.5)) +
  ds_spectrogram(wl = 200, collevels = seq(-50, 0, 1)) + ds_oscillogram()

# dark theme with other axis titles
x <- x + ds_theme(xlab = "Time of the song (s)")

# restore the previous theme
ds_set_theme(old)
